t: Abbas came to the throne of a divided Iran, its provinces held in part by the Ottomans and the Uzbeks and its court ruled by quarrelling Qizilbash factions, and he went on to rule it at its military, political and economic height.

He weakened the Qizilbash with a standing army and civil service of Georgian, Circassian and Armenian slave-soldiers, the ghulams, and with it retook Khorasan, the Caucasus and Mesopotamia, while his armies killed and deported tens of thousands in Georgia.

He moved the capital to Isfahan and rebuilt it, yet in his last years he had one son killed and two others blinded, and the Cambridge History of Iran blames the practice for the poor statesmanship of later shahs.
dyk: Abbas shaved off his beard at nineteen, keeping only his moustache, and so set a fashion in Iran; when an Ottoman ambassador made arrogant demands, he had the man's beard shaved and sent to the sultan.
ev: Abbas is born in Herat, the third son of Mohammad Khodabanda, governor of Khorasan
He has Murshid Qoli Khan, who had put him on the throne, killed after a banquet and rules in his own right
The Treaty of Constantinople cedes Azerbaijan, Shirvan, Dagestan and Tabriz, among other lands, to the Ottomans
He defeats the Uzbeks near Herat and moves his capital from Qazvin to Isfahan
The Iranians win a decisive victory over the Ottomans at Sufiyan, near Tabriz
Abbas has his eldest son, Mohammad Baqer Mirza, murdered at Rasht
With four English ships he retakes Hormuz from the Portuguese and takes Kandahar from the Mughals
Abbas dies at Farahabad; his grandson succeeds him as Shah Safi

f.born: 27 January 1571 in Herat, Khorasan; third son of Mohammad Khodabanda and Khayr al-Nisa Begum, of the Safavid dynasty
f.died: 19 January 1629 at his palace in Farahabad on the Caspian coast; buried in Kashan
f.role: Fifth Safavid shah of Iran, titular governor of Herat as a child, shah until his death in 1629
f.known: the ghulam corps and the new standing army; the defeat of the Uzbeks and the Ottomans and the reconquest of lost provinces; the deportations and massacres in Georgia and Armenia; the capture of Hormuz with English help; the new capital at Isfahan; embassies to Europe; the killing and blinding of his sons
